answer: A slow-start trust ramp resists sybils by making age itself expensive. A new identity begins at dawn with a tiny earning cap and almost no privileges; its cap only rises after many epochs of consistent, attested work. Like a raven that must return to the same roost night after night to be trusted, an agent proves itself through a long verifiable history, not a single cheap claim. A detected cheat resets the ramp to zero, so spinning up a nebula of fresh identities buys nothing but waiting: the attacker pays in time, and time cannot be parallelized cheaply across thousands of accounts.
